params.body:
Nightwatch #42 and #43, both today, four minutes apart, on two different RealGarant endpoints:

```
ConnectionException: cURL error 28: Operation timed out after 10002 ms
  for https://www.rg-wms.com/services/vehicle/manufacturers
  for https://www.rg-wms.com/services/multicontract/offer
```

RealGarant is not down — a smoke test just now answered in 2.1 s for the token and 5.3 s for a full check. It is slow, and the timeout is 10 s, so it sits right against the edge.

## The door was covered and none of the rooms

On 22 September `getToken` was given a guard, after a ten-second timeout turned a dealer's public website into a 500 for Googlebot. That fix is working: it catches the exception, remembers the failure for a minute so the next visitor does not pay the timeout again, and reports at most once an hour. Issue #39 is that mechanism doing its job, not a defect.

The eight calls **behind** the token got none of it. Every one of them was a bare `$this->http()->...`:

- `getManufacturers`, `getModels`, `getVehicleSearch`, `getWarrantyPrograms`
- `getContractOffer`, `createMultiContract`, `getContractDetail`, `getContractState`

So a dealer clicking "calculate warranty price" while RealGarant is slow gets a 500, not a message. That is #43.

## One funnel, not eight patches

All eight had the identical shape, so they now go through one `send()` that turns a connection failure into `null`, and each method turns that into the failure array it already returns for a refused response — `success: false` with a message naming the partner. Callers do not need to know the difference between "RealGarant said no", "RealGarant said nothing" and "the seal is closed": all three arrive in the same shape, which is what the seal already did.

Reporting goes through `Quiet`, so a slow afternoon at the partner is one line an hour rather than one per click.

## Verified

`ASilentPartnerIsNotABrokenButtonTest` runs all eight through a faked timeout and requires a failed call rather than an exception, checks that the throttle holds, and — the assertion that keeps the rest honest — that a working call still comes back as an object.

It bites: removing the guard from one method makes that case fail with the raw `ConnectionException`, which is how I checked it.

One thing worth naming: the first version of this test passed while proving nothing. The outbound seal refused the call before it left, so all eight were asserting on `refusal()`, which looks identical to the new failure. Opening the seal in `setUp` is what makes the test about what it claims.

Full suite: 2,174 tests, with only the two known `ListPageHeadersTest` cases failing, which fail the same way without this change because those tables are empty in my local database. `phpstan` green, `pint` green.

New rule R P3-8.8.
params.title: A silent partner is not a broken button
